environment.bitsandbytes_availability: Not installed. Natively requires NVIDIA/CUDA for Windows, or ROCm for Linux. Unsupported on AMD Windows out-of-the-box.

hardware_and_backend.backend_available: CPU only (installed PyTorch is +cpu; torch_directml is missing; ROCm is unsupported natively on Windows)

feasibility_analysis.qlora_explanation: QLoRA relies on bitsandbytes for 4-bit NormalFloat quantization, which is heavily optimized for NVIDIA CUDA. It does not support AMD GPUs on Windows.
feasibility_analysis.lora_explanation: Standard LoRA on CPU (using System RAM) is the safest route to avoid 4 GB VRAM OOM errors and driver incompatibility. A 0.6B model trained on CPU will be slow but will successfully fit within the 16 GB system RAM.
feasibility_analysis.expected_vram_ram_requirements: CPU RAM: ~8-10 GB (Model + Optimizer States + Gradients + Activations). VRAM: N/A (Using CPU). If AMD DirectML were forced, 4 GB VRAM would almost certainly OOM during training.
feasibility_analysis.risk_of_oom: Low risk of RAM OOM (16 GB is sufficient). High risk of VRAM OOM if GPU training were attempted.

recommendations.precision: float32 (or bfloat16 if CPU supports it efficiently)

estimates.training_time_for_900_examples: 10 - 24 hours (CPU training is significantly slower than GPU)

conclusion.summary: Standard QLoRA is not feasible due to AMD/Windows limitations. The safest alternative is standard LoRA running on the CPU.
conclusion.next_steps: Install PEFT and TRL, and execute a CPU-based LoRA training loop to avoid driver/VRAM issues.
